events.title: British Parliament Abolishes the Slave Trade
events.description: The Slave Trade Act 1807 received royal assent, making the transatlantic slave trade illegal throughout the British Empire. It prohibited the trading of enslaved people, though slavery itself continued in British colonies until 1833.
events.significance: A landmark step in the global abolitionist movement, it led Britain to use its navy to suppress the slave trade and paved the way for the later abolition of slavery in the empire.

events.title: Greek War of Independence Begins
events.description: Traditionally dated to March 25, Bishop Germanos of Patras is said to have raised the banner of revolt at the monastery of Agia Lavra, signaling the start of the Greek uprising against Ottoman rule.
events.significance: The revolt led to the establishment of an independent Greek state and is celebrated annually as Greek Independence Day, inspiring other nationalist movements in Europe.

events.title: Triangle Shirtwaist Factory Fire
events.description: A fire broke out at the Triangle Shirtwaist Factory in New York City, killing 146 garment workers, mostly young immigrant women. Locked exit doors and inadequate fire escapes contributed to the high death toll.
events.significance: One of the deadliest industrial disasters in U.S. history, it spurred major reforms in workplace safety laws, fire codes, and the growth of labor unions.

events.title: Treaty of Rome Signed
events.description: Six nations, Belgium, France, Italy, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, and West Germany, signed the Treaty of Rome, establishing the European Economic Community and Euratom.
events.significance: The treaty laid the foundation for the modern European Union by creating a common market and deepening economic integration in postwar Europe.

events.title: Selma to Montgomery Marches Conclude
events.description: Led by Martin Luther King Jr., thousands of civil rights marchers reached the Alabama State Capitol in Montgomery after a five-day march from Selma, demanding equal voting rights for African Americans.
events.significance: The march built momentum that helped secure passage of the Voting Rights Act of 1965, a milestone in the American civil rights movement.
